Resolves #18162

`buildScripts/util/check-theme-surfaces.mjs` gates its own CI workflow and `npm run check-theme-surfaces`, and has had no unit coverage since `c623b2f63c`. This adds 20 arms over the three contracts it still owns — parity, token-only consumption, completeness — plus the fail-closed empty-surface guard.

The deleted 618-line spec is deliberately **not** restored. It describes a 734-line guard; the surviving one is 217 lines, because the Institution token language took the `--fm-*` skin parity, the contrast floor and the drawer-frame seam with it. A verbatim restore would have red-lined on the majority of its arms for reasons unrelated to whether the guard works.

Evidence: L4 (mutation-proven unit arms against the real export) → L4 required (#18162's ACs are all unit-observable; the guard is a pure function over files). Residual: none.

Micro-review eligible: test-only — one new spec file, no source change; the diff adds coverage and alters no behavior.

## AC Evidence
| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/util/check-theme-surfaces.spec.mjs` — 20 passed under `npm run test-unit` |
| AC-2 | positive arms per family: `[surface]` ×1, `[parity]` ×4, `[token-only]` ×4, `[completeness]` ×2 |
| AC-3 | exemption arms: `modeInvariant`, `var()` fallback, custom-property declaration, line comment, block comment, quoted string, component-local token |
| AC-4 | `an alias whose referent differs is not byte-identical` + its falsifier `an alias whose referent is identical in both skins still fails` |
| AC-5 | every fixture is written under `fs.mkdtempSync(os.tmpdir())` and removed in `afterEach`; no repository theme file is read |
| AC-6 | five mutations, counts in **Test Evidence** below |
| AC-7 | spec header names the dropped Institution-era checks and why |

## Deltas from ticket
Two arms beyond the ticket's list, both from reading the subject rather than the AC text: `every SCSS file below the view root is walked, not just the top level` (pins the `walkScss` recursion — a non-recursive walk would silently stop guarding nested panes), and the `[completeness]` one-skin case, which reports against the *other* skin and is a different code path from the undefined-in-both case.

## Test Evidence
All arms run in CI. The mutation controls do not, so their receipts are here — each mutation was applied to the guard, the suite run, then `git checkout --` restored it (`git status` verified clean after every round):

| mutation | red | green |
|---|---|---|
| `[parity]` byte-identical push removed | 2 | 18 |
| `[token-only]` literal detection disabled | 4 | 16 |
| `resolvesDifferently` forced to `false` | **1** | 19 |
| `[completeness]` dark-skin push + `[surface]` fail-closed guard disabled | 2 | 18 |

The third row is the one worth reading: exactly one arm names the alias escape hatch, and it is the arm that would have caught #17200's *"parity rule flags correct aliases"* regression.

The nine exemption arms assert emptiness, so they correctly cannot detect a disabled check — that asymmetry is why the positive arms are counted separately in AC-2 rather than reported as one total.

# PR Micro-Review

**Class:** mechanical — test-only. 244 lines of arms over a guard that gates its own CI workflow and has had no coverage since `c623b2f63c`. No source touched.

**Verdict:** Approved — 0 required actions.

**Glance:** The first thing worth checking on a spec-for-a-tool is whether it exercises the tool or a copy of it, and this does the former: `await import(modulePath)` resolves the real `buildScripts/util/check-theme-surfaces.mjs` and calls its actual export, `collectThemeSurfaceFailures` (`:145`). A spec that reimplemented the guard's parsing would pass forever while the shipped guard rotted, and that failure mode is invisible in a green run — so it is worth verifying rather than assuming. **20 arms, 20 passed** at `9b34b7266a` in an isolated worktree.

Declining to restore the deleted 618-line spec is the right call, and the reasoning is the valuable part: it described a 734-line guard, the surviving one is 217 lines, and the Institution token language took the `--fm-*` parity, the contrast floor and the drawer-frame seam with it. A verbatim restore would have red-lined on most of its arms **for reasons unrelated to whether the guard works** — worse than no coverage, because it teaches the next reader the guard is broken when the spec is merely describing something that no longer exists. Twenty arms against what the guard owns today is the honest replacement.

The `L4` claim holds rather than being inflated: the guard is a pure function over files, so a temp-dir fixture plus the real export is the strongest evidence available here, not a stand-in for a browser.

One thing worth knowing given tonight: this is the second guard-without-coverage traced to the same commit — `check-theme-surfaces` lost its spec at `c623b2f63c`, and this repo's substrate-size enforcement has been gone since then too. That commit removed the received Brain implementation and took more enforcement with it than its diff made obvious. Not this PR's problem; worth a sweep for whatever else lost coverage there.
